questions.text: A global company must keep its application available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. Which architectural strategy best meets this requirement?
options: Move all data to Amazon S3 Glacier
Deploy the application across multiple Regions with data replication between them
Deploy the application across multiple Availability Zones within one Region
Use only instances Spot to reduce costs
questions.explanation: Multiple Availability Zones protect against localized data-center failures, while a multi-Region architecture with appropriate data replication is required to tolerate the loss of an entire Region.

questions.text: An organization is reviewing the Performance Efficiency pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Which practice is most closely aligned with this pillar?
options: Use the right resource types and technologies for each workload and evolve choices as new technologies become available
Restrict root access and enable MFA for every account
Apply billing tags to every resource
questions.explanation: The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, selecting appropriate resource types and continuously reviewing technology choices as workloads and AWS capabilities evolve.

questions.text: A company adopts a multi-cloud strategy using AWS and another cloud provider at the same time. Which common disadvantage should it consider?
options: Increased operational and management complexity across different platforms
questions.explanation: Multi-cloud strategies can increase operational complexity because teams must understand multiple platforms, tools, security models, billing systems, and integration patterns.

questions.text: A company with multiple AWS accounts wants centralized security guardrails that prevent member accounts from disabling AWS CloudTrail even if a member-account administrator attempts to do so. Which AWS capability enables this control?
options: IAM policies applied independently in each account
AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs)
questions.explanation: The Service Control Policies (SCPs) of the AWS Organizations define maximum permissions for member accounts, allowing blocking actions such as disabling CloudTrail throughout the organization.

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, when a customer uses Amazon RDS as a managed database service, who is responsible for patching the underlying operating system used by the managed database infrastructure?
options: AWS, because Amazon RDS is a managed service
No patching is required for managed services
questions.explanation: For managed services such as Amazon RDS, AWS manages more of the underlying infrastructure stack, including operating-system maintenance and patching, while the customer remains responsible for areas such as data, access configuration, and workload-specific settings.

questions.text: A company must encrypt data at rest in Amazon S3 and retain granular control over the creation, rotation, access policies, and auditing of the encryption keys. Which option best meets this governance requirement?
options: Client-side encryption only, with no AWS key-management service
Do not encrypt and rely only on IAM controls
SSE-KMS using an AWS KMS customer managed key
SSE-S3 using Amazon S3 managed keys
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed AWS KMS key provides granular control over key policies and permissions and supports auditing of key usage through AWS CloudTrail.

questions.text: A compliance team must ensure that all Amazon EBS volumes in an account remain encrypted and wants continuous detection when a resource becomes noncompliant. Which AWS service is most appropriate for this continuous configuration evaluation?
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously records and evaluates supported resource configurations against rules, making it suitable for detecting noncompliant resources such as unencrypted EBS volumes.

questions.text: A critical transactional database running on an Amazon EC2 instance needs persistent low-latency block storage and point-in-time backup capability through snapshots. Which AWS service should be used?
questions.explanation: Amazon EBS provides persistent block storage for EC2 instances, including low-latency volume types suitable for transactional workloads and snapshot support for backup and recovery.

questions.text: A company wants to orchestrate Docker containers in production with managed scaling and native AWS integrations while avoiding management of Kubernetes control-plane infrastructure or EC2 worker fleets. Which combination is the most appropriate?
options: AWS Direct Connect with Amazon Route 53
Amazon EC2 without a container orchestrator
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS provides AWS-native container orchestration and AWS Fargate provides serverless compute for containers, allowing teams to run container workloads without managing the underlying EC2 server fleet.

questions.text: A company must migrate petabytes of data to AWS but has limited internet bandwidth. Which AWS offering is designed for large-scale offline or physical data transfer?
questions.explanation: A AWS Snow Family (including Snowball) provides physical devices to transfer large volumes of data to AWS without depending on the bandwidth of the internet.

questions.text: A company wants dedicated private network connectivity between its on-premises data center and AWS with more consistent bandwidth and network performance than an internet-based connection. Which AWS service should it use?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity from customer locations to AWS and can deliver more consistent network performance than connections that traverse the public internet.

questions.text: A global enterprise wants an AWS Support plan that includes a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), proactive guidance, and the highest level of support for mission-critical workloads. Which support plan provides these capabilities?
questions.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support provides designated TAM engagement, proactive guidance, architectural and operational support, and the highest standard support tier for mission-critical workloads.

questions.text: A global e-commerce company is planning its AWS migration strategy and needs its applications to scale automatically for seasonal traffic peaks such as Black Friday without overprovisioning resources. Which AWS Cloud benefit is most relevant to meeting this requirement efficiently and economically?
options: Elasticity, which allows resources to be provisioned and deprovisioned dynamically and automatically according to demand.
Global economies of scale, which allow AWS to offer lower prices because of its large customer base.
Security, which protects application data and infrastructure against cyber threats.
Agility, which enables rapid development and deployment of new features and services.
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the cloud's ability to increase or decrease resources dynamically to match demand. This is critical for handling seasonal traffic spikes without permanent overprovisioning, optimizing both cost and performance.
questions.hint: Think of the cloud's ability to adapt resource capacity quickly as workload demand changes.
optionRationales: Global economies of scale help reduce overall AWS pricing but do not directly describe automatic scaling for sudden traffic peaks.

Elasticity is the cloud's ability to increase or decrease resources dynamically to match demand. This is critical for handling seasonal traffic spikes without permanent overprovisioning, optimizing both cost and performance.
Agility refers to the ability to innovate and release products quickly. It is important, but it does not specifically describe automatic capacity changes for seasonal traffic peaks.
Security is fundamental in AWS, but it is not the cloud benefit directly associated with automatically scaling resources to match seasonal traffic demand.

questions.text: A traditional bank is moving part of its infrastructure to AWS but must keep sensitive customer data and legacy systems in its own data centers because of strict compliance and latency requirements. It still wants to use AWS compute and analytics capabilities as part of the overall environment. Which cloud deployment model best fits this scenario?
options: Hybrid cloud, integrating on-premises infrastructure with AWS Cloud resources and services.
Public cloud, migrating all resources and data to AWS infrastructure.
Private cloud, building only an internal data center with cloud-like virtualization technologies.
Multicloud, using AWS and another public cloud provider for different workloads.
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with public-cloud resources. It allows the bank to keep sensitive or legacy workloads locally while integrating them with AWS services and scalability. Services such as AWS Outposts can support hybrid architectures.
questions.hint: The company must keep some workloads on premises while still using public-cloud capabilities.
optionRationales: A pure public-cloud model would not meet the requirement to keep sensitive data and legacy systems on premises.
A private-cloud-only approach would not achieve the desired integrated use of AWS public-cloud compute and analytics capabilities.

The Hybrid Cloud is the ideal model, as it allows the company to maintain data and applications sensitive on-premises (in its private data center) while taking advantage of the services and scalability of the public cloud of AWS, connecting the two environments safely and efficiently. AWS Outposts are examples of solutions for this scenario.
Multicloud refers to using multiple cloud providers and does not specifically address integration between on-premises infrastructure and AWS.

questions.text: A technology startup is developing a new mobile application and needs an environment that supports rapid experimentation, continuous feature deployment, and quick scaling for unpredictable user growth while avoiding large upfront hardware investments. Which AWS Cloud advantage is most critical to this startup's success?
options: Enhanced security by using AWS security controls and experience.
Replacing CapEx with OpEx to reduce upfront capital spending.
Agility, allowing the startup to innovate, experiment, and deploy features quickly without slow infrastructure procurement.
High availability and fault tolerance so the application can remain online during component failures.
questions.explanation: Agility allows organizations to experiment, provision resources quickly, and release products and features faster. That speed is especially valuable to startups that need rapid iteration and continuous deployment.
questions.hint: Focus on how quickly the startup can develop, test, and launch new capabilities.
optionRationales: Moving from CapEx to OpEx is an important financial advantage, but rapid experimentation and deployment are more directly tied to agility.
Security is essential but is not the main cloud advantage enabling frequent experimentation and rapid feature delivery.

Agility allows organizations to experiment, provision resources quickly, and release products and features faster. That speed is especially valuable to startups that need rapid iteration and continuous deployment.
High availability is important for production applications, but the scenario emphasizes rapid experimentation, deployment, and response to growth, making agility the primary benefit.

questions.text: A manufacturing company is migrating its ERP systems to AWS. The CFO is particularly interested in how this affects infrastructure investment. What is the primary change in cost model that AWS offers compared with maintaining an on-premises data center?
options: Convert operating expenses (OpEx) into capital expenditures (CapEx), requiring large upfront hardware investments.
Eliminate all IT costs because AWS manages everything.
Increase CapEx because annual software licenses must always be purchased upfront.
Convert much of the infrastructure CapEx into variable operating expenses (OpEx), paying for consumed cloud resources instead of large upfront hardware purchases.
questions.explanation: A core cloud financial benefit is reducing large upfront infrastructure CapEx and moving toward variable operational spending based on consumption. Organizations pay for cloud resources as they use them rather than purchasing all required physical capacity in advance.
questions.hint: Compare purchasing physical infrastructure upfront with consuming infrastructure as an operational service.
optionRationales: AWS generally reduces the need for upfront infrastructure CapEx rather than increasing it.
This reverses the typical cloud financial model: AWS shifts much infrastructure spending from CapEx toward OpEx.
A core cloud financial benefit is reducing large upfront infrastructure CapEx and moving toward variable operational spending based on consumption.
AWS manages underlying cloud infrastructure, but customers still incur IT and cloud operating costs. Cloud adoption changes the cost model rather than eliminating all costs.

questions.text: A data-analytics company processes large volumes of IoT sensor information in real time and requires high availability and low latency. It deploys the solution across several Availability Zones within a single AWS Region. What is the primary benefit of this design?
options: Failure isolation and high availability within the Region, protecting the application from the loss of a single Availability Zone.
Lower cost because multi-AZ deployment is inherently cheaper than single-AZ deployment.
Compliance with data-sovereignty laws in multiple countries.
Access to AWS services that are unique to each Availability Zone.
questions.explanation: Availability Zones are physically separate and isolated locations within a Region. Deploying across multiple AZs helps an application remain available if one AZ experiences a failure, improving regional resilience and fault tolerance.
questions.hint: Think about why AWS Regions contain multiple isolated Availability Zones.
optionRationales: Multi-AZ architectures often cost more because resources are duplicated; the primary benefit is resilience, not lower cost.
Availability Zones are physically separate and isolated locations within a Region. Deploying across multiple AZs helps an application remain available if one AZ experiences a failure.
Data-sovereignty requirements across countries generally involve Region selection, not multiple AZs within one Region.
Availability Zones in a Region provide access to the Region's service portfolio; their main architectural value is isolation and resilience rather than unique service catalogs.

questions.text: A development team is applying the AWS Well-Architected Framework and is focused on right-sizing resources, adapting capacity to demand, avoiding unnecessary spending, and selecting efficient pricing models over time. Which pillar is being prioritized?
questions.explanation: The Cost Optimization Pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs, providing adequate resources (right-sizing), taking advantage of efficient pricing models (such as reserved forums and Savings Plans) and scale to meet demand in an economic way. This aligns directly with efficient provisioning, adaptation to demand and cost optimization..
questions.hint: Think of the pillar concerned with using resources economically and eliminating waste.
optionRationales: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems effectively, including automation and operational processes, rather than primarily on resource spending.
Security focuses on protecting information and systems rather than cost-efficient provisioning and pricing.

The Cost Optimization Pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs, providing adequate resources (right-sizing), taking advantage of efficient pricing models (such as reserved forums and Savings Plans) and scale to meet demand in an economic way. This aligns directly with efficient provisioning, adaptation to demand and cost optimization..
Reliability focuses on recovery from failures, resilience, and continuity rather than financial efficiency.

questions.text: A global media company needs to deliver high-quality video to users on multiple continents with the lowest possible latency. It wants content cached close to end users to improve streaming performance. Which component of the AWS global infrastructure is designed specifically for this purpose?
options: Edge Locations, which cache content and serve requests close to users.
Local Zones, which extend an AWS Region into selected metropolitan areas.
Availability Zones, which are isolated locations within an AWS Region.
AWS Regions, which are geographic areas containing multiple Availability Zones.
questions.explanation: Edge Locations are points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver content closer to end users around the world, reducing latency for content such as video and images.
questions.hint: Think of the infrastructure that sits at the edge of the AWS network for content delivery.
optionRationales: AWS Regions host core regional services but are not the global edge-cache layer designed to place copies of content near users around the world.
Availability Zones provide resilience and fault isolation inside a Region but are not the global content-cache points used to reduce delivery latency.
Edge Locations are points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache and deliver content closer to end users around the world.

Local Zones extend a region AWS for specific metropolitan locations for applications that require ultra-low latency for local users. Although they reduce latency, their focus is to extend the computer services and database, not the delivery of cache content globally as the Edge Locations.

questions.text: A software development company has a legacy monolithic application that runs on-premises servers. They want to migrate this application to the AWS to take advantage of the scalability and resilience of the cloud, but they do not have the resources to completely rewrite the application code. However, they want to make some modifications to optimize the use of managed services from AWS, as the replacement of a self-managed database by a Amazon RDS. What is the migration strategy of the '6 Rs' from AWS is the most suitable for this scenario?
options: Refactor/Re-architect, rewriting most of the application to use cloud-native architecture.
Replatform, making limited cloud optimizations without changing the application's core architecture.
Rehost, moving the application exactly as it is with no meaningful changes.
questions.explanation: Replatform, also known as 'Lift-Tinker-and-Shift', is the strategy of migrating the application to the cloud by making some optimizations to take advantage of the native cloud resources (such as replacing a self-managed database with Amazon RDS), without rewriting the main code. This fits perfectly in the scenario described.
questions.hint: Think of the migration strategy that permits limited cloud improvements without a full rewrite.
optionRationales: Rehost would move the application with little or no modification, while this scenario explicitly includes adoption of a managed service such as Amazon RDS.

Replatform, also known as 'Lift-Tinker-and-Shift', is the strategy of migrating the application to the cloud by making some optimizations to take advantage of the native cloud resources (such as replacing a self-managed database with Amazon RDS), without rewriting the main code. This fits perfectly in the scenario described.
Refactor/Re-architect involves major redesign or rewriting to take full advantage of cloud-native patterns, which the company cannot afford here.
Retire means decommissioning an application that is no longer needed, which is not the company's objective.

questions.text: An online gaming company needs extremely low latency for multiplayer users in a specific city. The nearest AWS Region is still too far away. Which AWS global-infrastructure capability can place selected AWS compute and storage services closer to users in that metropolitan area?
options: AWS Outposts, which installs AWS infrastructure in the customer's own facility.
Availability Zones, which provide resilience within an AWS Region.
AWS Local Zones, which extend selected AWS services into specific metropolitan areas for low-latency workloads.
Edge Locations, which are primarily used for global content caching and delivery.
questions.explanation: Local Zones are a type of infrastructure AWS extending a region AWS for specific metropolitan locations, allowing customers to execute applications that require ultra-low latency for close end users, such as online games, using services AWS as EC2 and EBS.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS infrastructure extension created specifically to bring compute closer to a city outside the main Region footprint.
optionRationales: Edge Locations are primarily used for content caching and delivery through services such as CloudFront rather than for running general EC2-style application infrastructure.
AWS Outposts brings AWS infrastructure into a customer's own site, not into an AWS-operated metropolitan extension for nearby end users.

Local Zones are a type of infrastructure AWS extending a region AWS for specific metropolitan locations, allowing customers to execute applications that require ultra-low latency for close end users, such as online games, using services AWS as EC2 and EBS.
Availability Zones provide fault isolation within an existing Region but do not solve latency caused by geographic distance from that Region.

questions.text: A financial-services company is designing an AWS application that will process highly confidential customer data. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar should be the primary focus for protecting that information and meeting regulatory requirements?
options: Cost Optimization, to make data protection economical.
Security, focused on protecting information, systems, and assets.
Operational Excellence, to automate operational response processes.
Reliability, to keep the system available.
questions.explanation: The Pillar of Security AWS Well-Architected Framework is the most relevant to protect confidential data, manage access, implement security controls, encryption and ensure regulatory compliance, which are the main concerns for a financial services company.
questions.hint: Which pillar deals directly with protecting information and systems?
optionRationales: Cost Optimization is important, but protecting confidential information and meeting regulatory obligations primarily belong to the Security pillar.
Operational Excellence includes automation and incident-response practices, but the broader protection and compliance objective belongs to Security.
Reliability addresses availability and recovery. Those matter, but the central requirement here is confidentiality and regulatory protection.
The Security pillar focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets and is the primary Well-Architected pillar for this scenario.

questions.text: A rapidly growing SaaS company wants to deploy new production features several times a day with minimal disruption, monitor systems proactively, and identify and resolve operational problems quickly. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar most directly addresses these objectives?
questions.explanation: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems effectively, automating operational processes and deployments, observing workloads, responding to events, and continuously improving procedures.
questions.hint: Think of the pillar centered on operational automation, observability, and continuous improvement.
optionRationales: Performance Efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet performance requirements rather than primarily on deployment processes and observability.
Cost Optimization focuses on financial efficiency and avoiding unnecessary spending, not frequent reliable deployment and operational monitoring as its core objective.

Reliability helps workloads withstand and recover from failure, but the scenario's emphasis on deployment automation, monitoring, and operational response maps most directly to Operational Excellence.
Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems effectively, automating operations, responding to events, and continuously improving procedures.

questions.text: A financial-services company is designing a high-volume transaction application that must recover automatically from server or Availability Zone failures while minimizing downtime and data loss. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar should be the primary architectural consideration?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar focuses on a workload's ability to perform its intended function consistently, recover from failures, acquire resources to meet demand, and mitigate disruptions.
questions.hint: Think of which pillar of Well-Architected Framework deals directly with the resilience and ability of a system to recover from failures.
optionRationales: Performance Efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, not primarily about recovery and resilience.
Reliability focuses on performing the intended function consistently and recovering from failures, directly matching this scenario.
Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary spending rather than designing for failure recovery.
Operational Excellence covers how systems are run and improved, but Reliability is the core architectural pillar for automatic recovery and minimizing disruption.

questions.text: A biotechnology startup with limited financial resources wants to use highly specialized AI and machine-learning services to analyze large genomic datasets. It could not afford to build all of the required infrastructure and sophisticated models independently. Which AWS Cloud advantage helps make these advanced technologies economically accessible?
questions.explanation: AWS's global economies of scale allow the provider to spread the cost of sophisticated infrastructure and managed technologies across a very large customer base, making advanced services such as AI/ML accessible without each startup building the full stack itself.
questions.hint: Consider how AWS's enormous operating scale lowers the barrier to using sophisticated technology.
optionRationales: Agility accelerates innovation and experimentation but does not directly explain why expensive advanced technology becomes economically accessible to a small company.
Elasticity helps resources match demand, but it is not the main concept explaining access to sophisticated AI/ML capabilities without large upfront infrastructure investment.
Global economies of scale allow AWS to provide advanced technology at a cost that would be difficult for an individual startup to reproduce independently.
Security is a major cloud benefit, but it is not the primary economic mechanism enabling affordable access to advanced AI/ML services.

questions.text: A large retail company has a legacy stock management system that has been built on a monolithic architecture and is becoming difficult to maintain and scale. They want to modernize this application for a microservices and serverless architecture on AWS, making the most of the native cloud services, such as AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB, to improve scalability, resilience and innovation capacity. '6 Rs' from AWS is the most suitable for this scenario?
questions.explanation: Refactor/Re-architect redesigns how an application is built so it can take advantage of cloud-native capabilities such as microservices and serverless services. It usually requires substantial code and architecture changes.
questions.hint: Which migration strategy involves the largest architectural change to adopt cloud-native patterns?
optionRationales: Rehost moves the application with little or no change and would not achieve the planned microservices and serverless modernization.

Replatform involves moving the application to the cloud and making some optimizations to take advantage of the cloud's resources (e.g. migrating from a self-managed database to Amazon RDS), but does not imply a complete rewrite for a microservices and serverless architecture.
Refactor/Re-architect substantially redesigns the application to use cloud-native patterns such as microservices and serverless services.
Retain means keeping the application in its current environment and would not meet the modernization objective.

questions.text: A multinational company operates in several countries and must keep customer data within the required geographic jurisdictions. Which AWS global-infrastructure component is fundamental when choosing where regional compute and storage resources and their data will reside?
questions.explanation: AWS Regions are separate geographic areas containing multiple Availability Zones. Region selection is a fundamental architectural decision for controlling where regional workloads and data are hosted to support data-residency and compliance requirements.
questions.hint: Think of the broadest AWS geographic unit selected when deciding the primary location of regional workloads and data.
optionRationales: Availability Zones are isolated locations inside a Region. They provide resilience but do not represent separate broad geographic jurisdictions for data residency.

Edge Locations are used to store cached content and reduce latency for end users, as part of services such as Amazon CloudFront. They are not designed to host the main application infrastructure or to meet data residency requirements in different countries.
AWS Regions are separate geographic areas that allow customers to choose where regional workloads and data are hosted.
Local Zones extend selected services closer to metropolitan areas but remain associated with a parent Region and are not a substitute for Region-level data-residency decisions.

questions.text: A traditional company's CFO is evaluating migration to AWS and wants to understand the effect on cash flow. Instead of making large upfront investments in hardware and software that depreciate over time, the company would pay recurring charges based on actual cloud usage. What is the primary cost-model change?
options: Move from OpEx to CapEx to obtain more predictable fixed annual costs.
Move from CapEx to OpEx, replacing large fixed-asset investments with variable consumption-based operating expenses.
Increase mandatory annual fixed costs because AWS always requires long-term contracts.
Eliminate all IT costs and move to a zero-cost operating model.
questions.explanation: Cloud adoption can reduce the need for large upfront CapEx purchases and replace much of that infrastructure spending with variable OpEx based on actual service consumption, improving cash-flow flexibility.
questions.hint: Compare purchasing assets upfront with paying for infrastructure as an on-demand operating service.
optionRationales: This reverses the usual cloud transition. AWS reduces the need for infrastructure CapEx and supports a consumption-based OpEx model.
Moving from CapEx to OpEx converts large upfront fixed-asset investments into variable operating expenses aligned with actual consumption.
Cloud computing does not eliminate all IT costs; customers still pay for the services and resources they consume.

Although there are options for long-term contracts (such as Savings Plans or Reserved Instances) which can reduce costs, the fundamental model of the cloud is payment by use, which is inherently variable and flexible, not an increase in mandatory annual fixed costs.

questions.text: A manufacturing company wants to reduce the environmental impact and carbon footprint of its IT operations while moving to AWS. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar should be the primary focus when designing workloads to use resources efficiently and reduce environmental impact?
questions.explanation: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads, including improving utilization, reducing unnecessary resource consumption, and choosing more efficient technologies and managed services.
questions.hint: Which Well-Architected pillar addresses environmental impact directly?
optionRationales: Cost optimization may indirectly reduce environmental impact by reducing waste, but its primary objective is financial efficiency.
Performance Efficiency is about using resources efficiently to meet technical performance requirements and is not primarily an environmental-impact framework.
Reliability focuses on resilience and recovery rather than environmental sustainability.
Sustainability directly addresses environmental impact and efficient resource consumption in cloud workloads.

questions.text: A small consulting company is moving to AWS and wants to understand its responsibilities under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model. In a public-cloud workload where the customer manages EC2 instances and application data, which statement best describes the customer's responsibility for security IN the cloud?
options: The customer is responsible only for paying for services; AWS handles all security responsibilities.
AWS is responsible for all security, including customer firewall configuration and data protection.
The customer is responsible for areas such as guest operating-system configuration, application security, network controls, identity permissions, and protecting its data.
AWS and the customer are responsible equally for every security layer with no defined boundary.
questions.explanation: This statement is correct. The client is responsible for cloud security, which includes operating system configuration and management, applications, customer data, network configurations (such as Security Groups and Network ACLs), and data encryption. AWS takes care of cloud security, i.e. the physical infrastructure, hardware, software and network that performs the services of AWS.
questions.hint: Separate AWS's responsibility for the cloud infrastructure from the customer's responsibility for what it deploys and configures in the cloud.
optionRationales: Customers retain significant security responsibilities for what they configure and run in AWS; paying for the service does not transfer all security responsibility to AWS.

This statement is correct. The client is responsible for cloud security, which includes operating system configuration and management, applications, customer data, network configurations (such as Security Groups and Network ACLs), and data encryption. AWS takes care of cloud security, i.e. the physical infrastructure, hardware, software and network that performs the services of AWS.
The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud, including workload configuration, identities, applications, data, and guest operating systems where applicable.
The model defines a division of responsibility rather than making AWS and the customer equally responsible for every layer.

questions.text: A SaaS company operates in a highly competitive market where releasing new features and responding quickly to customer demand are essential. It needs developers to experiment, deploy to production several times per day, and adjust infrastructure quickly without long procurement cycles. Which AWS Cloud advantage is most critical in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Cloud agility lets teams experiment, provision environments quickly, release features frequently, and respond rapidly to market changes.
questions.hint: Think about the cloud's ability to support rapid innovation, experimentation, and continuous delivery.
optionRationales: Economies of scale reduce provider costs but do not directly enable rapid feature iteration.
Security is essential but does not primarily describe fast experimentation and deployment.
Elasticity adjusts resource capacity to demand, while the broader ability to innovate and deploy quickly is agility.
Agility enables rapid experimentation, frequent releases, and fast response to market needs.

questions.text: An engineering company has a set of legacy simulation software that depend on highly specialized hardware and expensive software licenses, which are not compatible with the cloud AWS. In addition, these systems have an expected lifespan of just more 12 months before they are completely replaced by a new solution. Given the complexity and cost of rewriting or adapting these systems to the cloud, what migration strategy of the '6 Rs' from AWS would be the most appropriate for these specific systems?
questions.explanation: Retain means keeping an application in its current environment when migration is not currently justified because of technical dependencies, incompatibility, cost, or short remaining useful life.
questions.hint: Choose the strategy for systems that should remain where they are for now rather than be migrated immediately.
optionRationales: Rehost is not suitable because the specialized dependencies are incompatible and migration effort is not justified.

Withdrawal means to disable systems that are no longer needed. Although the system has a limited service life, it is still required by 12 months. The strategy of 'Retreat' would be applied after replacement, not during the phase of migration planning.
Repurchase would require an available replacement product and does not address the short-term need to keep this specialized system running.
Retain keeps the workload on premises until replacement or a future migration decision becomes practical.

questions.text: A large technology company has hundreds of accounts AWS, managed by different teams and departments. They are facing significant challenges to accurately track and allocate costs, identify unused resources and ensure that expenses are aligned with the budgets of each project. What practice, aligned with the Cost Optimization Pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework, it would be more effective to solve these problems of visibility and cost governance?
options: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to identify underutilized resources and apply cost allocation tags.
Deploy every critical application across multiple Availability Zones.
Migrate all instances EC2 for instance Spot to drastically reduce computing costs.
Configure the AWS CloudTrail to monitor all calls from API and user activities.
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags help attribute spending to teams and projects, while tools such as Trusted Advisor can identify underutilized resources and cost-optimization opportunities.
questions.hint: The problem is both cost attribution and waste detection. Use financial labels plus optimization recommendations.
optionRationales: Combining cost allocation tags with optimization recommendations improves ownership, visibility, and waste reduction.

The AWS Trusted Advisor can identify underutilized resources (part of cost optimization). The application of cost allocation tags (Cost Allocation Tags) is a fundamental practice to track and allocate costs to different projects, teams or cost centers, improving visibility and cost governance in a multi-account environment.

Although the instances Spot can reduce costs, they are suitable only for workloads tolerant of failures and do not solve the fundamental problem of visibility and allocation of costs in a complex environment with multiple teams and budgets.

The AWS CloudTrail is an essential tool for auditing, compliance and security, recording the actions carried out in the account AWS. Although important for general governance, it is not the main tool or the most effective practice for tracking and allocating specific costs.

questions.text: During the strategic planning phase for mass migration from a traditional bank to the cloud, the executive leadership seeks to align the training of development teams with new governance and security methodologies, aiming to reduce organizational risks and accelerate the transition. AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF), which perspectives should be specifically prioritized to empower people and modernize decision-making and governance processes?
questions.explanation: The Perspective of People of the AWS CAF focuses on the development of skills, training and cultural change of teams, while the perspective of Governance orchestrates migration programs, portfolio management and measurement of business value.
questions.hint: The AWS CAF group its guidelines into six organizational perspectives: three focused on business/person skills and three focused on technical skills.
optionRationales: The Perspective of People of the AWS CAF focuses on the development of skills, training and cultural change of teams, while the perspective of Governance orchestrates migration programs, portfolio management and measurement of business value.
Operational Excellence directly addresses operational automation, observability, and continuous improvement.
Cost Optimization focuses on financial efficiency.

The official perspectives that make up the AWS CAF are divided into Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations; 'Architecture' and 'Strategy' are not official framework perspective names.

questions.text: A mission-critical monolithic order-processing application experiences volatile traffic. The engineering team wants to decouple request intake from backend processing so bursts can be buffered until workers consume them. Which architecture best improves resilience and elasticity?
options: Use horizontal compute scaling and asynchronous decoupling with Amazon SQS.
Use vertical scaling on tightly coupled EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.
Use Route 53 geolocation routing with synchronous network mirroring.
Use instances EC2 Spot configured with data persistence in shared Forum Store volumes.
